title: Stability baiting & keystone client notes
content:
Context:
- Goal: surface fragile interactions early by nudging a tiny, high-value subset of clients ("keystones") through new model/config flips. Not a full canary — this is intentionally targeted 'baiting' so we get representative edge cases without exposing broad traffic.
- Why: past full-cohort canaries diluted noisy signals; keystone clients trigger hard-to-reproduce failure modes (long sessions, heavy KV usage, extreme token lengths).

Foundational constraints / assumptions:
- Keystone cohort must be <= 0.5% of global traffic and split across regions (NA/EU/APAC). Prefer customers we can contact quickly (SLAs, CSMs).
- Runtime flags available: model_variant, kv_cache_mode (full/prefix-only/disabled), continuous_batching (on/off).
- Observability: p50/p95/p99 latency per-client, token-generation-rate, kv-miss-rate, kv-load-latency, error-rate (5xx + model-invalid-output), user-visible failures (client reports in CS).

Planned micro-experiment (sequence):
1) Day 0: identify 8 keystone clients (mix of 3 heavy-conversation, 3 long-seq batch, 2 high-parallel tenants). Notify CSMs + set expectation window (48h).
2) T+0h: route 0.1% of each client's traffic to new model_variant=A (A is quantized-prod-s9, identical routing). Keep kv_cache_mode unchanged.
3) T+30m: observe. If p95 latency increase > 25% or 5xx rate diff > +0.3% (absolute) => revert immediately.
4) T+2h: bump to 0.25% (if stable). Monitor KB-cache miss trajectories (we expect transient spike).
5) T+6h: bump to 0.5% if stable. Hold 24h for overnight coverage.

Primary signals and thresholds (early-warning):
- Latency: p95_client > baseline_p95 * 1.25 => FLAG
- Error spike: delta_5xx_abs >= 0.3% OR relative increase > 200% if baseline tiny => FLAG
- KV miss slope: sustained increase in kv_miss_rate > 0.5pp (percentage points) for 15m => investigate cache keys/TTL combos
- Regression: evaluation prompt set score drop >= 2.5% => FLAG (automated eval runs on each bump)
- Backpressure on serving nodes: queue_depth > 75th percentile historical by > 40% => consider throttling batching

Rollback ladder (fastest first):
- Route-level rollback: flip traffic for the keystone cohort back to previous model_variant (instant feature flag).
- Safety throttle: reduce per-client traffic to 0.01% then to 0%.
- Node isolation: if a node group shows saturation, move affected traffic to other AZs/tiers.
- Hotfix: redeploy prior runtime image if the issue is traced to kernel selection (requires SRE).
- Postmortem trigger: any outage impacting > 1% global or any keystone client SLA breach -> full postmortem and exec notice.

Operational runbook snippets (quick commands / notes):
- Check cohort mapping: curl -s "https://console.redwood/api/v1/rollouts?cohort=keystone-A" | jq .
- Force-flip: POST /api/flags/flip {"route":"keystone-A","model_variant":"v_prev"}  (ops token)
- Telemetry quick query: 
  - latency baseline: influxql "SELECT percentile(latency_p95,95) FROM requests WHERE client IN (...) AND time > -6h"
  - kv miss delta: prometheus query delta(kv_miss_total[15m]) / delta(kv_requests_total[15m])

Open questions / unknowns to investigate before next run:
- Are keystone clients using long-lived sessions that hold expired KV keys? Need to audit client session reuse patterns (ask infra for session traces).
- How does our KV prefetch behave for quantized models with different kernel selection? We saw a subtle mismatch in staging last month. Reference PR: github.com/redwood/inference/PR/1352.
- Can we make the rollback flip a single-API call in the SDK so product owners can self-serve rapid rollback? (proposal: SDK flag endpoint with authenticated audit)

Hypothesis-driven experiments to add later:
- Toggle kv_cache_mode=prefix-only for keystones and compare token-level latency vs. full cache (short A/B).
- Introduce delayed-batching window (50ms -> 70ms) for keystone cohort only to see if throughput smoothing reduces 99th tail.
- Probe model-variant gradations: vA (quantized s9), vB (int8+kv-optimized), vC (float16 baseline) to map latency vs. quality curve per client.

Personal notes / reminders:
- Call Diego before Day 0 to confirm cohort list & CSM contact details.
- Add a small slack alert in #rollouts: @oncall if FLAG fired.
- Draft short email template for affected customers (CSM) — two variants: "FYI, doing low-risk test" and "We observed regressions and reverted".
- Capture sample failing transcripts if FLAG triggers (store in /tmp/keystone-fails/<client>/).

Quick retrospective checklist after run:
- Was there a single point of failure? (Y/N)
- Which signals tripped first? (latency / errors / kv)
- Did automated evals flag quality drop? (attach eval id)
- Did CSM escalation happen? (time, channel)
- Action items for infra/runtime/product (assign owners + due dates)

Notes to self: keep the experiment surgical. The name "baiting" is intentionally provocative — reword to "targeted keystone probe" before sharing externally. This doc is my running brain-dump; will refine into a shareable short-runbook if the experiment gives high signal.

-- Asha
